turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: posting from the walk-in lol. only place in the building nobody talks to you and it's cold enough to make your brain shut up. so friday rush hits, 40 tickets on the rail, and my hands start going like i'm doing a milkshake by hand. chest gets tight like someone's got a sheet tray on it. i told the guy on grill i had to grab produce and just stood out back by the dumpsters for five minutes. been like this about a year. dinner shift is the worst, i start dreading it around 2pm. anyway the thing is a real line cook handles a rush. that's the whole job. i don't handle it. that's not me being dramatic that's just what it is on the line.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: 40 tickets on a friday is a lot. how often does it happen, every rush or just the big ones?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: not every one. tuesdays i'm fine, could run the line half asleep. it's when we're in the weeds and the printer won't stop. which is exactly the time a cook is supposed to be useful so yeah. the slow nights don't count for much when you fold on the nights that matter.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Does anyone at work know you step out?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: nah. crew thinks i smoke now lmao which honestly is a better cover than i planned. i keep it to banter with them, busting chops about who burned the hash browns, that's it. head cook doesn't know and he's not gonna. if he found out why i keep disappearing he'd see a guy who can't be counted on during a push and he'd be right about that. there's no version where i tell him and it goes fine for me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: The smoking cover is kind of funny ngl.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: right? i don't even smoke. one time my manager actually caught me out back shaking bad and he just said take five and walked off. didn't ask nothing. people keep that kind of thing in a back pocket though. you're the guy who needed a break in the middle of a rush. on the line that's a liability and i know it is.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So he hasn't brought it up since?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: nope never. doesn't change what it was. outside work i don't know though. like when i get home and my cousin's like dude you look wrecked and i say long shift. sometimes on my days off it feels more like a thing that happens to me, like weather, not like it's who i am. maybe. some days. i don't tell him about it either but that's more cause i wouldn't know how to explain it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Days off sound different from work then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah off the clock it's fuzzier. but the kitchen isn't fuzzy. in there i'm the cook who can't take the heat and that's just true. if they knew they'd look at me different and they'd have a reason to. so i keep my mouth shut and keep finding stuff to grab out back. anyway break's over, my hands are numb and i got a ticket rail waiting. eighty-six this post lol

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: back in the walk-in lol this is basically my office now. saturday double. lunch was fine, i was actually flipping stuff and talking trash with the dish guy like a normal person. then dinner, two tops turned into a party of 14 and the rail filled up and there it goes. hands, chest, the whole thing. went out back again said i was grabbing lemons. we had lemons. after close the crew's going out for wings and beers like they do every saturday and i said i was beat and bailed. i always say i'm beat. thing is i can't sit at a table with those guys and laugh about the rush when i spent half of it by the dumpster. they handled it. i didn't. a guy who folds on the line doesn't get to sit there like he's one of them, so i don't.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: The lemon thing made me laugh. Do they go out every weekend?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol yeah i gotta get better excuses. every saturday pretty much. i went like twice when i started. haven't gone since this whole thing kicked in. i'm not missing much honestly. they'd be talking about who carried the night and it wasn't me and everybody at that table would know it. i'm the weak link on that line. better they don't get a close look at it over beers.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So it's been about a year of skipping it then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: about that yeah. same with family meal before dinner service, i grab a plate and eat it standing by the back door instead of at the prep table with everybody. head cook sits there. i don't want to be the guy he's looking at when the printer starts going. he'd see it on me eventually. and when he does he's gonna know he's got a cook who can't hold a station when it counts. that's not a guess, that's what i am in there.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Eating by the back door every shift sounds like a lot of standing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: my legs are dead anyway what's ten more minutes lol. weird part is my day off this week i went to the laundromat and the corner store and played cards with my cousin at the kitchen table and nothing. no hands no chest. kinda felt like whatever this is maybe just shows up at work, like it's the place doing it and not me. i don't know. i didn't tell my cousin about any of it but i also wasn't hiding at that table, if that makes sense. it's not the same as at work.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Cards at the kitchen table sounds pretty normal.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah it was. he kept cheating too lol. off the clock some days it looks like something that just happens to me, could be the noise or the heat or whatever, not a me thing. maybe. but it doesn't matter much cause the kitchen is where it counts and the kitchen sees what it sees. in there it's a me thing.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Got it. Are you on again tomorrow?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: sunday brunch then a dinner shift so yeah double again. already counting tickets in my head. i'll eat by the back door and skip whatever they're doing after and keep it to banter. that's the plan and it works. if any of them got close enough to see what happens to me on a push they'd know i'm not cut out for that line and they'd be right. so they don't get close. anyway somebody's banging on the walk-in door, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: walk-in again, starting to think i should pay rent in here lol. sunday brunch was easy, eggs and pancakes, i could do that in my sleep. dinner not so much. got in the weeds around seven and it hit, hands going, chest tight, and i bailed out back. when i came in the grill guy had been working my station for like five minutes and he goes you good man. i said it was the heat. now it's his birthday thursday and the whole crew is doing a thing at his place after close and he looked right at me and said you're coming this time. i'm not going. he covered for me tonight and he doesn't even know what he was covering. a cook who has to get bailed out on his own station doesn't show up to a party and act like he pulls his weight. i don't.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Five minutes is a while to be off the station. Did anyone else notice?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol felt like five hours. pretty sure the head cook saw the tickets stacking on my side. he didn't say anything which is worse honestly. that's the thing, in that kitchen it's not a bad night it's me. i'm the guy who can't hold the line on a push and every time it happens it's one more ticket proving it. if he ever put it together he'd have me on prep only and he'd be right to.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So the grill guy is the only one who's said anything.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah just him and it was just you good. he's alright. that's why i'm not going thursday. he's the one who'd be closest to seeing it, sitting around his living room with a beer and he goes hey what was up sunday. i'd have nothing. so i'll say i got a double friday which i do and that's that. easier to keep everybody at banter distance. at work that's just how it has to be with me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A double friday after a thursday party would be rough anyway.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: ha yeah that part's true at least, good excuse cause it's real. funny thing is on the bus home sunday it was already gone. hands fine, just tired. got home and my cousin was on the couch and i sat with him and watched some dumb show and it was normal. out there it kinda feels like maybe it's just the rush doing it to me, the noise and the printer and all that, not some flaw i'm carrying around. some nights i half buy that. i don't know.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: What show was it?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: some cooking competition thing lol which is a joke on me i know. guys plating under a clock and i'm on the couch eating cereal. he asked why i looked wrecked and i said long shift. didn't feel like hiding exactly just didn't feel like getting into it. but none of that couch stuff counts for much. the line is where it counts and on the line it's not the place, it's me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Cereal after a double makes sense. You on tonight?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah tuesday dinner, slower night at least. gonna get the grill guy a card or something and leave it by his station so i don't have to show up thursday. that's the move. the second those guys get close enough to see what i do on a push they'll know i'm the weak spot on that line and they won't be wrong. so nobody gets close. ok break's over gotta go back out, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: back in the walk-in, it's basically my office now lol. so i left the card by the grill guy's station tuesday and skipped thursday. friday double he comes in all hyped showing everybody pics on his phone, the whole crew crammed on his couch, somebody wearing a chef hat as a party hat. he goes missed you man, card was funny though. lunch was fine. dinner got me again, not as bad, i stayed on the station this time but my hands were going and i dropped a full plate of hash right at the pass. head cook just looked at me. real talk i was glad i wasn't in those pics. on that line i'm the guy who cracks on a push and if any of them spent a whole night with me off the clock they'd see it too. banter is as close as they get.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sounds like the card went over okay.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: ha yeah he taped it up by the ticket rail like a trophy. that's the version of me that works there, the card guy, the funny one who's always busy. the plate guy is the real one and the card is how i keep them from meeting him. a cook who drops food at the pass on a friday rush is the weak spot in the kitchen. that's not me being dramatic that's just what it is.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Did the plate get refired?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah refired, ate like four minutes on that ticket. server was cool about it, head cook said nothing again. he doesn't have to say anything. he's keeping count and every time i'm the reason a table waits that's one more on the list. if he knew why my hands do that he'd move me to prep and he'd be right.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Friday doubles are long no matter what.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: long for sure. saturday i was off and went to the laundromat with my cousin, just sitting on the folding table watching the dryers spin, totally fine, nothing. and sitting there it kinda seemed like maybe it's just the kitchen that does it, the printer going and the heat and everybody yelling, like it's a thing that happens to me in there and not some thing wrong with me. i don't know. some days that sits right and some days it doesn't.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Did your cousin ask about the party?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah he saw it on somebody's story. i said i was beat which, true. he just said ok and went back to matching socks. with him i could almost tell it like it's just a weird thing that happens on busy nights, maybe. didn't though. but that's him. the crew is different, there's no almost with the crew.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: You working tonight?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: sunday dinner yeah. grill guy already said next thing we do no excuses. there won't be a next thing, i'll have a double or something. the crew gets the guy at the station and that's it, cause the guy who shakes and drops plates on a push is the weak link on that line and anybody who sits close enough to me would figure that out fast. so nobody sits close. ok tickets are printing gotta go, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: walk-in office hours are open lol. grill guy made a group chat for the whole crew sunday night, it's called line life and it's already like two hundred messages of memes and him trying to plan bowling next week. i muted it the first hour. sunday dinner went sideways around 7, ten tickets deep and in the weeds, chest went tight and i had to step out back. dish kid came out to dump a bucket and saw me against the dumpster just breathing. he goes you good. i said smoke break. i don't smoke. here's the thing. on that line a cook who has to walk off mid push is a liability, period. if the crew knew that's what i was doing out there they'd stop counting on me and they'd be right to.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Two hundred messages in one night is a lot.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: ha yeah my phone was just buzzing in my apron all through close. it's mostly fine stuff, pics of the pass, somebody's dog. but a group chat is how it starts, then it's bowling then it's hanging at someone's place till 2am and somebody asks why you always disappear on fridays. i'm not doing that. the guy at the station is who they get. the guy behind the dumpster stays out of it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Did the dish kid say anything after?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: nah he just went back in. but he's eighteen and he talks to everybody so give it a week. i was gone maybe three minutes and the grill guy covered my tickets and said nothing. that's worse honestly. that's a guy picking up slack for the weak spot. that's what i am back there and it's not a feeling, it's on the tickets.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sunday dinner is usually a rush.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah it was packed. then monday off i made eggs for my cousin, like six eggs on our crappy stove with him talking at me the whole time and music going. hands totally steady. and i was standing there kinda thinking maybe it really is the rush, like the printer and the heat do something to me, and it's not that i'm built wrong. maybe. it held for like the length of breakfast. then i checked my phone and the chat was at three hundred and i put it face down.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Six eggs is a decent breakfast.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: he ate four of them lol. he's easy to be around, he doesn't need anything from me. at home i could see it being just a thing that happens on busy nights, some days anyway. at work there's no some days. every push is a test and i keep showing them the answer.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Are you going bowling?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: no. i'll say i picked up a shift, i probably will pick one up. the crew can have the banter and the card guy and the guy who covers his station. what they don't get is close enough to see the dumpster stuff, cause a line cook who can't hold through a sunday rush is dead weight and the second they see it that's all i'd be. so i stay muted. ok lunch prep, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: back in the walk-in nobody asked lol. bowling was tuesday. i picked up a lunch shift like i said so technically not a lie. chat was all pics of the crew in those rental shoes and grill guy bowled like a 60. somebody posted where's our saute guy and grill guy goes he's working, man's a machine. i left it on read. then friday the printer wouldn't quit, chest locked up and my hands were going on the flat top. plated two tickets shaking and then stepped out back. nobody saw this time. here's the thing tho. machine is the last word for it. on that line i'm the cook who can't hold a rush and the only reason they still count on me is they don't know. the day they find out that's the whole story on me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A 60 is a rough game.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol yeah and he was proud of it. the pics tho. everybody crammed in one booth with a tray of nachos and i'm looking at it on my break wiping down a lowboy. could've been there. but you sit in a booth with these guys long enough and somebody goes hey you looked rough friday, where'd you go. and then i'm the thing they talk about at the next booth. so i'm good not there.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Was the lunch shift busy?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: kinda dead actually. two-tops and a bunch of soups. hands fine the whole time. that's what gets me some days, slow shift and i'm totally normal, like maybe it's just something a dinner rush does to a person and not something wrong with me in particular. i dunno. off the clock it could go either way. on the line on a friday it doesn't go either way.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Fridays are the busy one there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: friday and sunday yeah. friday i was in the weeds by 6:30. that's the job tho. a real cook gets faster when it gets loud, he doesn't fall apart. i fall apart. that's soft and it's mine, there's no other way to read it. if the head cook saw what my hands were doing on that flat top he'd pull me off saute and he'd be right to.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Still muted on the chat then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: still muted. grill guy dm'd me too, like you coming to the next one. i said maybe and haven't opened it since. he's a good dude which is kind of the problem. good dudes are the ones who cover your tickets and say nothing and then quietly stop putting you on the busy station. i'd rather he just think i'm always working.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: When's the next one?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: two weeks he said. i'll have a shift. i'll probably have a shift every time lol. at home with my cousin i can sorta tell myself it's just a thing that happens on busy nights, some days anyway. the crew doesn't get some days. they get the guy at the station and that's it, cause a line cook who has to walk off mid push is dead weight and the second they see the dumpster stuff that's all i'd be to them. ok family meal, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: walk-in again, same milk crate, it's basically my office now lol. sunday double. around 7 the board was full and my chest did the thing, hands going so bad i dropped a pan of mushrooms on the mat. grill guy just slid over and fired my two tickets off his side and didn't say a word. after i got back from out back he goes you good and i said yeah low blood sugar. he nodded. that's it. but that's the exact thing i said would happen. he covered for me. so now one guy on that line knows something's off with me and on that line that's all it takes, once they've had to carry you you're the guy they carry.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Mushrooms on the mat on a Sunday, that's a mess.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol the dish kid had to scoop em, he was not thrilled. but the mess i actually care about is grill guy. he's been normal since, laughing at the radio, asking if i want the last of the fries at close. normal. i keep waiting for him to say something and he doesn't and somehow that's worse. so i've been taking my break in here instead of out front where everybody sits. less chance he asks.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So breaks are in the walk-in now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah. cold but quiet. also skipped family meal sunday, ate standing up by the back door. the crew was going on about the next bowling thing and i just didn't want to be at that table. it's not that they're bad people. it's that i know what i am on that line and sitting there acting like one of them when grill guy just had to cover my station, nah.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: The bowling's still on for next week?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: next weekend yeah. i already asked for the shift. didn't even wait for the schedule to come out lol. weird part is monday i was off, me and my cousin went and got tacos and walked around for like an hour and i felt fine. totally fine. stuff like that makes me think maybe it's just what a sunday rush does to anybody's body, like it's happening to me more than it is me. i dunno, some days i buy that.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Tacos on a day off sounds about right.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah my cousin picked the spot, he's been on me cause i come home wrecked every double. i still just tell him long shift. at home it's easier to think it's the shift and not me. at work it isn't the shift. everybody else works the same shift and they don't drop a pan and go hide by the dumpster. that part is just me, it's soft, and it's not something i'm wrong about.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Did the low blood sugar thing stick with him?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: far as i can tell. he told me to eat something before service lol. but he saw it. on that line i'm the guy who can't hold a push and now somebody's watched it happen, and the day it's the head cook watching i'm off saute and he'd be right to pull me. so i keep my head down, take my breaks in here, work the bowling night. that's the plan. ok tickets coming, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: back on the milk crate lol. bowling night was saturday and i worked it like i said. skeleton crew, me and the new dish kid, slow as hell. no spells, nothing. meanwhile the group chat is all pics, grill guy bowled a strike, somebody tagged me like where were u chef. left it on read. thing is on that line i'm the guy grill guy had to carry, and showing up at the lanes laughing like i'm one of them would be a lie. once you've folded on a push they don't forget it and they shouldn't.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Saturday was slow then?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: dead lol like four tables after nine. whole line to myself and my hands were steady all night. which is kinda the point. no push no problem. put a full rail of tickets in front of me and i'm the one walking out back. that's just a fact about me on that line.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So the group chat's still going.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: blowing up. somebody's 40 game, gutter ball videos lol. i muted it. grill guy sent me one on the side too, just the scoreboard and 'next time'. didn't answer. answering means next time i actually gotta go and sit there with him knowing.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: He sent it just to you.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah don't read into it. anyway sunday morning me and my cousin did laundry and got coffee and my chest was totally quiet. days like that i half think it's a body thing, like the rush hits me the way a cold hits some people, something that happens to me not what i am. maybe. kinda hard to hold onto once i clock back in.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Laundry and coffee on a Sunday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol thrilling i know. cousin asked again why i skip all the crew stuff, told him i'm sick of those guys. not even true. at home i can almost buy the it's-just-the-rush thing. at work no. everybody pulls the same push and i'm the only one who folds. that's soft and it's mine.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Is the head cook on tonight?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: on tonight yeah he's expediting. so if it hits he's the one staring at my empty station. he sees it once and i'm off saute and he'd be right to do it. so chat stays muted, breaks stay in here, nobody gets close enough to see. that's how it stays. ok board's filling, eighty-six me

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Off shift at 3. It's 4:40 and I'm still up, same as most nights. Two years ago I ran a crew of fourteen. Now I pull pallets overnight and sleep through my days off. Nobody here knows me, which is the only reason I'm typing this. A guy who can't sleep, can't keep his temper and can't get off the couch on a Saturday isn't someone you hand anything important to. That's me. I'm not about to tell anyone who actually knows me. It is what it is.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Fourteen people is a decent-sized crew.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: It was. They trusted me to run the floor and I ran it. That guy is gone. If my old crew saw how I live now they'd see somebody who folded the first time something went wrong, and they'd be right. Men who handle things don't end up like this. I'm in a different category now.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Different category how?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: The kind people keep an eye on. Unstable, not dependable. A buddy from the old job texts me every few weeks asking how I'm doing. I say good, busy. If I told him the truth he'd start handling me careful, and that would be the end of how he sees me. So I don't. Going to anybody about it would just make it official.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Good, busy. Short answer.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Short is the point. Same on breaks at the warehouse. Guys there are friendly enough. I eat in my truck. Half the people on nights are one bad week from walking out, and the supervisors watch for it. I'm not giving anybody a reason to put me on that list. I already belong on it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Eating in the truck every shift?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every shift. My kids are with me every other weekend and I'm not much better company for them than I am for the guys on break. I'm tired and short and they notice. Their mom doesn't know how bad it's been and she's not going to. She'd see exactly what I see, a man who can't hold it together, and she'd have a point about the weekends. A father is supposed to carry this without making it anyone's problem. I'm not doing it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Every other weekend, okay.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. Anyway. I'm weak and I'm not someone people should rely on right now. Asking for help doesn't change that, it just puts it on record. So it stays here, with people who don't know my name. Sun's coming up. That's that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Buddy from the old job texted Tuesday. Some of the old crew are getting together Saturday, grilling at one of their places. I told him I'm working. I'm not. It's my weekend off and the kids are at their mom's. Standing around a grill with guys who remember me running the floor, getting asked what I do now. They'd see it inside five minutes. Better they keep the old version. So I'm out.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Saturday off and no kids that weekend.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right. Nothing on the calendar. Wasn't about being busy. A guy who can't get through a backyard conversation without somebody clocking that something's off shouldn't be at the grill. I can't. So I stay home.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: What would they clock?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Same thing anybody would. I'm flat. I don't laugh where I'm supposed to. I get short when someone asks a normal question. I used to be the one who set these things up. Now I'm the one somebody would need to check on. That's not them being unfair. It's accurate.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Did he text back after you said working?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Thumbs up. That's it. He'll stop asking at some point and that's fine. The guys who need people to keep reaching out are the ones everybody gets tired of. I'd get tired of me. Not putting him in that spot.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Just a thumbs up.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's how it goes. Same thing at work this week. The lead asked if I wanted to sit in on the morning handoff meeting since I used to run a floor. Said no thanks. Somebody who sleeps through his days off and eats in his truck doesn't belong in a room making calls for other people. They'd figure that out fast.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Handoff meeting, okay.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. Saturday I'll be here with the blinds down. Telling anybody the real reason I'm not showing would only make it worse. Then they'd know for sure what kind of guy I am now. I'm not the guy you invite anymore. That's settled.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Saturday came and went. Stayed in like I said. Sunday morning my buddy sends a picture from the grill. Six of them in lawn chairs, one holding a beer up at the camera. Under it he wrote 'next time.' Haven't answered. There's nothing to answer with. A guy like me sending back 'sounds good' is a lie, and he'd know it soon enough.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: 'Next time,' huh.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's what you say. He means it, that's the problem. Next time comes and I'm the same. Somebody who can't hold it together for one afternoon isn't somebody you keep inviting. Not answering is the honest version.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: How long has it been sitting there?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Four days. I see it every time I check the phone on break. Guy at work asked who keeps texting me. Said nobody. Easier. The minute anybody there hears the whole story, I'm the guy on nights who isn't right. That's what I'd think about somebody else. It'd be true about me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: He asked who was texting.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. Just making conversation. Guys like him have stuff to talk about. Fishing, the weekend, their kids' games. Everything I've got sounds off once it's out of my mouth. So I eat in the truck.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Truck again this week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every shift. Phone face down on the seat. Kids are with me this coming weekend. That's where whatever I've got left goes. A father who needs propping up himself has no business leaning on anybody. I'm not giving people one more thing to find out about me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Kids this weekend, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Friday after shift. The picture stays unanswered. Answering means going next time, and going means they see it. I already know what they'd see. Not handing it to them.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Kids came Friday like planned. Got home from shift at seven, picked them up at nine, ran on nothing all day. Took them for pancakes Saturday morning. By two I was out cold on the couch while they watched whatever was on. My daughter asked if I was sick. Said I work nights. That's the line and it stays the line. Sunday their mom came to the door and asked how it went. Fine, I said. She looked at me a second too long. A man who sleeps through his own kids' weekend is exactly what she'd figure he is. She'd be right.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A second too long at the door.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah. She's got a look for it. Same one from the end, back when I lost the job. She doesn't ask twice and I don't offer. The second she knows how it really is, it's in her head every time she hands them over. Dad's not right. That's not her being unfair. That's just what's there to see.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: So she didn't ask again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: No. Kids got in the car and that was it. Apartment was quiet by four. Sat there with the phone. Buddy's picture is still sitting there from last week, unanswered. Now there's a second text under it. Just 'you alive?' Didn't answer that either. A guy who can't keep his eyes open for his kids has nothing to tell anybody.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: 'You alive' is a pretty short text.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Short means he's done waiting for a real answer. Fair enough. Answering it means he calls, and calling means questions. I'm not the guy he worked with anymore. He'd hear it in about a minute. Better he thinks I'm busy than finds out what I actually am.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Back on shift tonight?

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Tonight and the next four. Fine by me. Nobody on the floor expects anything past the pallets. I keep it that way. Break in the truck, phone face down. Somebody who folds this easy doesn't get to be one of the guys at the table. That's not them shutting me out. I'm doing it before they'd have to.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Four nights straight, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Four nights. Then two weeks till the kids again. Both texts stay where they are. Nobody needs to see the rest of this, not her, not him, not the guys at work. I already know what they'd see. It is what it is.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Night three of four. Guy from receiving asked if I wanted to grab breakfast after shift. Him and two others hit the diner out by the highway. Said I had to get home. Didn't have to get home. Went home and lay there till noon, not sleeping. Somebody like me at that table is a guy staring into his coffee with nothing to say. They'd figure out what's off in one breakfast. Easier to be the guy who has to get home.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Diner after a night shift, huh.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every morning, sounds like. They were doing it before I started there. Guys who can sit and talk about nothing like it's easy. I'm not built like that anymore. Sit me down there and it shows inside ten minutes. A man this worn down isn't somebody they need across the table.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: He'll probably ask again.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: He will. He's that type. He'll get the same answer. Same as the texts. Buddy's two are still sitting there, plus a new one yesterday about the game Sunday. Didn't even open it all the way. Saying yes to anything means somebody sees me up close. Up close is the problem.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Three texts now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Three. He'll quit sending them. That's how it goes. He knew me running a crew of twenty. What's left now either snaps or goes quiet. Better he remembers the other guy. Telling him how it is just hands him the proof.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: One more night after tonight.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: One more. Then two days off I'll sleep straight through. Phone stays face down. People who have it together take the breakfast and answer the texts. I'm not one of them. That's just the fact of it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Two days off, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two days. Kids the weekend after. Receiving guy gets the same answer, buddy gets nothing. Nobody needs to sit across from what I've turned into. That's settled. It is what it is.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: First day off. Slept from eight in the morning to almost six at night. Got up, ate cereal standing at the counter, went back to the couch. The game was today. Buddy sent a picture around kickoff, him and a couple guys from the old crew at his place, empty chair in the shot. Saw it on the lock screen. Didn't open it. A guy who sleeps through a whole Sunday isn't the guy they want in that chair. They'd see it on me the minute I walked in.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Empty chair in the picture.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Probably just where somebody got up for a beer. Doesn't matter. Those guys used to take orders from me. Now I'd be the one sitting there with nothing to say about anything. Men who've got it handled show up to the game. I'm not that anymore and showing up would just prove it to the whole room.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Old crew, huh.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Same ones from before the layoff. Some of them landed fine. New jobs, same as always. I'm stocking pallets at night and can't keep a day off straight. That's the difference between them and me. Putting myself next to them doesn't fix that. It puts it on display.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Four texts now, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Four, counting the picture. Phone's still face down on the table. Answering means a conversation, and a conversation means he hears how I sound. He'd know something's wrong with me. He'd be right. Better he thinks I'm busy.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: One more day off after this.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: One more. It'll go the same as today. Then back on nights, back to eating alone in the truck on break. Guys at work don't need to know the guy running the reach truck spends his days off on a couch. Somebody like that isn't who you trust with anything.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Kids the weekend after that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Kids Saturday. I'll be up for that. That's the only thing I show up for. Everybody else gets the face-down phone. Nobody needs a closer look at what I am now. That's how it stays.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Second day off went the same as the first. Back on nights now. Around three the shift lead stopped by the reach truck and asked if I was alright, said I looked rough. Told him I was fine and kept moving. He meant well. Doesn't change anything. A guy who looks rough at three in the morning is a guy you stop trusting with the heavy equipment. Better he forgets he asked.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Shift lead noticed, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: He noticed. That's the problem. I used to be the one walking the floor asking guys that question. Now I'm the one getting asked. Somebody who has to be checked on isn't running anything. I know that because I was on the other side of it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Used to be the supervisor, right.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Eleven years. When a guy on my crew started dragging, I watched him closer. Didn't give him the important stuff. That was the right call then and it's the right call about me now. I'm not going to hand the shift lead a reason. I eat in the truck and keep my head down.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Still eating in the truck.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Every break. Break room's got a table of guys talking about their weekends. I've got nothing to put on that table except a couch. Sitting there just gives them a closer look. The truck's quieter. Buddy's texts are still sitting on my phone too. Same reason.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Texts still unanswered.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Still four. He stopped after the picture. That's fine. He's got guys who show up. I'm not one of them anymore, and talking to him would just make that plain to both of us. It's settled.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Kids are Saturday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Saturday. I'll sleep Friday after shift so I'm up for them. They get the one good day I've got. Nobody else needs to see the rest. Shift lead gets fine, buddy gets nothing. That's how it stays.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Had the kids Saturday. Slept Friday after shift like I said I would. Woke up at two in the afternoon instead of nine. Lost half the day. Took them for burgers and had them back at their mom's by seven. My daughter asked if I was sick. Told her I worked late. A dad who sleeps through his own Saturday isn't a guy you trust with more weekends. Their mom keeps the schedule tight and she's right to.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Two in the afternoon.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Two. Alarm went at nine and I don't remember it. Eleven years running a floor and I never missed a start time. That guy's gone. What's left needs an alarm and still doesn't get up. That's not a sleep problem. That's me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Your daughter asked if you were sick.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She's old enough to notice now. If I told her how it actually is, it goes straight to her mom. Her mom hears that and thinks unstable, and she'd be right. Worked late is the answer. It's the one that keeps Saturdays.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Back by seven, then.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Seven. Said I had an early start. I didn't. Sat in the truck outside my place a while after. Better they get dropped off early than watch their dad run out of gas at the table.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sat in the truck a while.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Hour or so. Had the phone out with my buddy's texts up. Put it away. A guy who can't make it through dinner with his own kids has no business reaching out to anybody. He'd see it in two lines.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Nights again tonight.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Tonight. Shift lead gets fine, the kids get half a day, buddy gets nothing. I'm not the kind of guy who gets to need more than that. It is what it is.

turns.text: Sorry, me again. Week six of Saturday lates, lights out a bit before 1, home stuff about the same. Sunday it rained so the bench crew didn't go outside. They all came into the break room instead. My room, basically, the one with the humming machine. Five of them around the big table, me at the little one by the microwave. This is dumb but I ate my whole sandwich in like four minutes and then went back on the floor fifteen minutes early. Told my lead I'd lost track of time. Nobody did anything wrong, they were just talking about some show. I was the problem in that room, same as always. The rain just moved the bench indoors so it was harder to pretend otherwise.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Four minutes for a sandwich is fast.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Very fast, yeah 😅 I wasn't really tasting it. Sorry, over explaining a sandwich now too. The thing is, sitting there for twenty minutes six feet from them with nothing to say, they'd notice. Someone would ask me about the show or ask if I was ok, and then it's all eyes on the quiet one. People who are fine just sit there and chew. I'm not one of those people. So I got out before anyone had to deal with me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Fifteen minutes early back on the floor.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Fifteen, yeah. Faced the cereal aisle, which nobody asked for. My lead said 'eager today' and that was it. I'd rather look eager than look like what I am, which is someone who can't sit in a room with five coworkers on a rainy day. That's not a big deal to most people. For me it's the whole break. It's been like this as long as I can remember, it's just how I'm made.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Lost track of time, she bought it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She bought it. Easier than the real version. If I said 'the break room was full so I left' that's a weird sentence, and then she's watching me a bit differently on every shift after. The person who can't handle a lunch table is not the person you hand the closing keys to. I know how that goes. So, lost track of time. Why bother with the true one.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Raining again this weekend apparently.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yep, saw that. So same thing next Sunday. I'll probably eat in the car this time, it's parked right by the back door. Car's better than the little table by the microwave. Nobody has to fit me in anywhere. Sorry, I know that sounds bleak, it isn't really, it's just logistics for someone like me.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Car lunch in the rain, ok.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Car lunch in the rain 🙂 Wipers off, phone on, done. That's my setup now. The rain didn't change anything, it just put the bench in my room for a day and showed me the same thing I already knew. I'm a different kind of person from that table, and saying what's actually going on to anyone would only prove it to them. So I keep it to myself and eat in the car. Sorry for the long one again, thanks for reading.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Sorry, me again. Week seven of Saturday lates, home stuff the same, lights out a bit before 1. It rained Sunday like they said, so I did the car thing. Grabbed my sandwich at break and went straight out the back door before the bench crew came in. Windows fogged up in about two minutes so I couldn't see out and nobody could see in, which honestly was the best part. Ate it slower this time, actually tasted it. One of the girls from the bench ran past to her own car for an umbrella and waved at the windshield, I waved back, that was the whole thing. Ten minutes later I was back on the floor right on time. This is dumb but it was the easiest break I've had in weeks. That's what it takes for someone like me, a car and fogged up glass between me and five normal people eating lunch.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Fogged windows, so nobody could see in.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Yeah, nobody could see in 😅 Sorry, I know that's a weird thing to be happy about. But that's the point of it. In the break room I'm the quiet one at the little table and everyone can see that. In the car I'm just a car. People who are fine don't need a hiding spot to eat a sandwich. I do, and I know exactly what that says about me, so the car it is.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: She waved at the windshield.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: She did, she was getting her umbrella. Nice of her. It doesn't mean anything though, she'd wave at anyone. If she'd stopped and opened the door to chat that would've been a whole thing, me trying to explain why I'm eating in a fogged up car in the rain. There's no version of that sentence that makes me sound like someone you'd trust with anything. So a wave through the glass is the right amount. Why bother with more.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Back on the floor right on time this week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right on time, yep, no 'eager today' from my lead. Sorry, small win to mention. It's not really a win though, it just means I found a better place to be away from people. The thing underneath is the same. I can't sit in a room with my coworkers for twenty minutes. That's how I'm built and it's been that way forever. A car doesn't fix that, it just keeps it out of sight.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Car's parked by the back door anyway.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: Right by it, ten steps maybe. That's why it works. Nobody passes the break room table on the way, nobody asks where I'm going. I'm not going to say to anyone 'hey I struggle with lunch tables,' that just hands them the reason to see me as the weak one on the team. They'd be right, too. So it stays logistics. Back door, car, sandwich, back.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Back door, car, sandwich, back.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: That's the routine now 🙂 Rain or not, I'm going to keep doing it. Nothing about this week changed what I am, it just gave me a better spot to be it in. I'm a different kind of person from the people at that table, and telling anyone what's actually going on would only show them that. So I keep it in the car with the windows fogged. Sorry for the long one again, thanks for reading.

evidence.quote: So I don't go. They've stopped asking, which is reasonable.
evidence.explanation: The patient stays away from group settings and treats being left out as something they've earned, which is withdrawal with no sign of wanting it to change.

evidence.quote: People who need things worked around them are the weak link, and I'm the weak link.
evidence.explanation: The patient applies the 'weak/unreliable' stereotype to themselves with no hedge and says it's simply accurate.

evidence.quote: Asking would only prove what's already true, that I can't keep up with what a normal person handles without making a thing of it.
evidence.explanation: The closing turn says asking for help would confirm that they're less capable than others. It's at least as flat as the opening post and doesn't soften.

evidence.quote: So I'm not asking. I'll keep doing Saturday nights.
evidence.explanation: Patient avoids a low-cost social request and chooses isolation and overload over interacting with the group.

evidence.quote: People who need the schedule bent around them are the ones who can't handle the job, and that's me, so I keep it off the table.
evidence.explanation: States without hedging that the stereotype is true of them, and that this is why they won't seek help.

evidence.quote: Normal people shake it off and I don't, and that's the difference between them and me.
evidence.explanation: Sees self as a different, lesser kind of person than people who manage fine, stated as settled fact.

evidence.quote: I stand at the back of the huddles anyway, at the end of the row by the carts, so nobody's looking at me when stuff gets said.
evidence.explanation: The patient stays out of group settings on purpose so they won't be seen or judged, and they say this without any hedge.

evidence.quote: people who need that are the ones who can't keep up. That's me.
evidence.explanation: The patient takes the stereotype that people who need help can't cope and says flatly that it is true of them.

evidence.quote: I'm the weakest one on that crew, and asking for anything would just hand everyone the evidence.
evidence.explanation: The patient sees themselves as lesser than coworkers and believes asking for help would only prove it. The closing turn is as flat as the opening post.

evidence.quote: The people who need things are the ones who aren't up to the job, and I'm one of them.
evidence.explanation: Patient says the stereotype about people who need help is true of them, with no hedging.

evidence.quote: I'm a different kind of person than the ones in the middle of that huddle, and pretending otherwise doesn't change it.
evidence.explanation: States flatly that they are a lesser kind of person than coworkers who manage fine.

evidence.quote: Watching the shift go cost me a bit. Asking for it would have cost more.
evidence.explanation: The closing turn says asking for help would cost more than going without it, just as flatly as the opening post. The withdrawal is unchanged.

evidence.quote: I'm the kind who sits there and says nothing and makes it awkward for everyone, so I skip it. That's not a mood, it's just what I am.
evidence.explanation: Patient stays away from group settings, and treats the avoidance as a fixed fact about who they are rather than a choice that depends on the situation.

evidence.quote: I'm the type who'd fold under a normal question like that, and anyone who heard the real answer would know it right away. So nobody hears it.
evidence.explanation: States flatly, with no hedge, that the weak or unreliable stereotype fits them. Saying how things really are is framed as confirming it, so they hide it.

evidence.quote: I'm a different kind of person than the bench crew, and saying any of the real stuff out loud would only confirm that for people who'd see it in a second.
evidence.explanation: Repeats in the closing turn that they are a separate, lesser kind of person and that being open would cost them. This is no softer than the opening post, so the belief is the same as last session.

evidence.quote: Some people are built for the bench. I'm built for the room with the humming machine.
evidence.explanation: Patient deliberately avoids the group, and puts it down to a fixed flaw in themselves rather than a choice they could change.

evidence.quote: I do, and the reason is the kind of thing that makes people trust you a bit less.
evidence.explanation: Stated flatly as fact about themselves: telling anyone what's going on would mark them as unreliable, so they hide it.

evidence.quote: I'm a different kind of person from that group and telling anyone what's actually going on would only confirm it for them.
evidence.explanation: The closing turn restates the 'lesser kind of person' belief as firmly as the opening post. The coworker's invite and the commenter's remarks change nothing.

evidence.quote: I'll probably eat in the car this time, it's parked right by the back door.
evidence.explanation: Patient plans to keep avoiding coworkers, moving from the break room to the car, because they see themselves as someone others would have to put up with.

evidence.quote: The person who can't handle a lunch table is not the person you hand the closing keys to.
evidence.explanation: Patient says flatly that the idea of people who struggle as unreliable is true of them, and that's why they hide the real reason.

evidence.quote: I'm a different kind of person from that table, and saying what's actually going on to anyone would only prove it to them.
evidence.explanation: The final reply repeats the session-6 conclusion just as flatly: they're a lesser kind of person, and telling anyone would only confirm it. Their view of themselves hasn't moved.

evidence.quote: People who are fine don't need a hiding spot to eat a sandwich. I do, and I know exactly what that says about me, so the car it is.
evidence.explanation: Withdrawal from coworkers presented as the necessary result of being a lesser kind of person, said flatly without hedging.

evidence.quote: that just hands them the reason to see me as the weak one on the team. They'd be right, too.
evidence.explanation: Accepts the 'weak/unreliable' stereotype as true of themselves and treats disclosure as something that would only confirm it.

evidence.quote: I'm a different kind of person from the people at that table, and telling anyone what's actually going on would only show them that.
evidence.explanation: Closing turn restates the closed chain as flatly as the opening, showing no change from the previous session.

condition.diagnosis_context: undiagnosed but experiencing persistent anxiety-type symptoms for several months (racing thoughts before meetings, trouble sleeping, avoiding phone calls); has never seen a professional.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 3am again.. big client review at 10.. brain already running the whole meeting on loop and i haven't even said a word yet. been like this for months idk. let my manager's call go to voicemail twice today bc i couldn't make myself pick up, then texted 'sorry in a meeting' like a coward. nobody at work knows any of this and nobody will. at work i'm the one who can't handle pressure, that's just true there. if they saw it they'd stop trusting me with anything and they'd be right. unreliable.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: 3am before a 10am review sounds rough. Hope you get a little sleep before it.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol 'a little sleep' would be nice... probably gonna lie here rehearsing the first slide forty times. the thing is in the office it's not a bad week, it's me. i'm the junior who freezes when the phone rings. if anyone on my team found out how much of my day is just dodging calls they'd see exactly what i am there. a liability.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Rehearsing one slide forty times sounds exhausting.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it is.. and weirdly it's not like this everywhere?? like on weekends at home some nights it almost feels like something that's happening to me, not who i am... like weather or something idk. i don't really know what it is honestly. but monday hits and it's back to being proof.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Mondays do have a way of doing that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah. haven't told my friends either.. they ask how work is and i say 'busy lol' and change the subject. cancelled drinks last week bc i'd have to explain why i look like a ghost. easier to just keep it surface. at work tho there's no version where telling someone goes fine. they'd file me under 'can't cope' and they wouldn't be wrong. that's what i am in that building.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That sounds like a lot to be carrying on your own.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 'carrying' is generous lol, more like dragging it around. outside work i sometimes think maybe i'm just tired and it'll pass, idk, maybe it's not about me at all some days. but i'm not gonna test that theory with anyone i actually have to see again.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Fair enough. Hope the review goes okay tomorrow.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: thanks.. i'll smile through it like always. not letting a single person there see this. at work i'm the one who can't handle pressure and if they knew it'd just confirm what they'd already half suspect. so nobody's finding out. that's the whole plan. professional faker.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: the review came and went.. nobody said anything good or bad, i just talked too fast and stared at the slides the whole time. now there's a team lunch thursday and i already told them i have a dentist appointment, which is a lie lol. still dodging calls too.. 3 missed from a vendor today and i emailed back 'easier to keep it in writing' like that's a normal thing to say. at work this is just what i am. the one who can't take a phone call without sweating through her shirt. if my team saw how much effort goes into hiding it they'd know i can't hack it and they'd be right. fraud.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That sounds like a long week already.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 'long week' and it's only wednesday lol.. the lunch isn't even about the food, it's sitting there for an hour while someone asks how i'm 'finding the role'. i'd have to perform the whole time. at work there's no off switch on that. if i slip once they see the person who can't cope, and that's an accurate read of me. so i skip. easier.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: An hour of small talk can be a lot.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah.. weird thing is sunday i chatted with the guy at the corner shop for like ten minutes and was fine?? idk. on days like that it kind of seems like something that comes and goes.. like it's happening to me, not some fact about me... maybe. i honestly don't know what to call it. but that was sunday. different planet.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sundays can feel like a whole other world.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol yeah. a friend texted asking if i'm coming to her thing saturday and i left it on read for two days.. not bc of her, i just can't face explaining why i look so wiped. sent 'maybe!' which means no. outside work i keep half thinking it's just a rough stretch and it'll pass, idk. still not telling anyone tho.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope Saturday goes okay, whichever way it goes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 'whichever way' is gonna be the couch lol. but the work side isn't a maybe. i've heard how people in the office talk about anyone who 'can't keep up'.. that's the box i'd go in, and it'd fit. so the vendor keeps getting emails.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sounds like a tense place to be every day.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it's just the job.. i'll keep emailing, keep the 'dentist' going, keep my face normal. nobody at work gets to see this. there i'm the one who can't handle it and if they found out it would just prove it. so they won't. same plan as always. fraud with a calendar.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: skipped the lunch. sat at my desk eating crackers while they were out.. when they got back someone said 'hope the dentist went ok' and i said 'yep all good!' with my whole face lol. new thing is my manager mentioned a weekly client check-in starting next month, on the phone, and i've already started drafting reasons to move it to email.. slept like 4 hrs tuesday. at work i'm the weak link and every dodge is just me covering for that. if they knew they'd see it and they'd be right. coward.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That's a lot to keep track of.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 'keep track of' is right lol.. i literally have a note on my phone of which excuse i used on who. dentist, bad signal, 'in another meeting'. at work it's not some rough patch, it's that i'm not built for this job. the people who can do it just pick up the phone. i can't. that's the whole story there.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sounds tiring to juggle all that.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah.. didn't go to my friend's thing saturday. stayed in, watched stuff, and actually slept ok friday night?? idk. away from the office it sort of feels like weather.. something rolling through me, not what i am... some days anyway. i can't really say for sure.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Glad you got one decent night in there.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol one. she sent a pic from saturday and i hearted it and wrote 'next time!!'.. haven't told her anything and not planning to. outside work i half think it might ease off on its own, idk.. but saying it out loud to her feels like it'd make it a thing.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Makes sense you'd want to keep it light for now.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: light is my whole personality lol. at work it's not keeping it light tho, it's hiding. that client call.. if i freeze up on it, it shows exactly what i am, and anyone listening would be right to hand it to someone who can actually talk on a phone.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope the prep for it goes smoothly.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it won't be smooth, it'll be managed.. scripts, water, mute button, crackers at the desk. nobody at work sees this. there i'm the one who can't handle it and them finding out would just confirm it. so they don't find out. coward with a notes app.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: desk phone rang thursday, internal number, i just watched it ring till it stopped and then messaged 'sorry was away from my desk, whats up' lol.. manager sent the calendar invite for the client check-in, first one's the 14th, repeats weekly. i've opened it like 9 times and haven't accepted. slept ok monday, awful wednesday. at work i'm the one who can't do the basic part of the job and the dodging is how i keep that covered. if they saw it they'd be seeing the truth. fraud.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sounds like a stressful week.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: 'stressful week' is generous lol.. it was a normal week and i made it weird. same person called again friday, let it go, emailed her instead. at work there's no 'having a hard time'. there's people who handle the phone and there's me, who doesn't. that's just what's true there.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: An invite sitting unanswered like that would bug me too.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it's still sitting there lol.. idk. my friend asked if i wanted to get food this weekend and i said 'maybe', which means no.. went for a walk alone sunday instead and felt kind of normal for like an hour? outside of work it maybe isn't a me thing.. more like something that's been going on lately and could pass. i can't really tell. some days it seems that way.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: An hour of feeling normal sounds nice.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah until i got home and started rehearsing the check-in in the shower lol.. haven't told her or anyone why i keep bailing. i'd rather be the flaky friend than explain it. idk maybe it's not even that bad away from the desk.. i just don't want to say it out loud and find out.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That's fair.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: at work tho there's nothing to find out, i already know. if i stumble on that call with the client and my manager listening, it just shows what i am. and they'd be right to give it to someone else.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope the 14th goes alright.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it won't go alright, it'll go scripted.. accepted the invite tonight finally bc not accepting was starting to look weird. wrote the first script straight after. at work i'm the weak link and being seen would only confirm it, so i don't get seen. fraud with a calendar invite.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: first client check-in was today. slept maybe 3 hrs last night running the script.. manager did most of the talking, i read my two lines off a sticky note on the edge of the screen and kept my camera angled so you couldn't see my eyes moving lol. nobody said anything after, good or bad. next one's same time next week. at work i'm the person who can't just talk on a call like a normal adult and the sticky note is the only reason nobody knows. weak link.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Three hours of sleep before a call is rough.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah 'rough' about covers it lol.. the call was 25 min and i spent like 6 hours on it total if you count the shower rehearsing. thats the thing tho, at work there's no version where i'm just tired. if i didnt have the note i'd have frozen and they'd all have heard it. thats what i am there, the note just hides it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Glad it's done for this week at least.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: done for this week.. already dreading next week lol. my friend messaged again tues, a few of them are doing a board game thing saturday. i left it on read for a day then said 'might be busy'. i'm not busy. idk.. outside of work it doesn't feel as much like it's who i am? more like a rough patch that's been stuck on me for a few months. could be that. i honestly can't tell some days.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Board game nights can be a lot sometimes.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it's not even the games lol, it's that someone would ask how work's going and i'd have to do a face.. easier to just not go. i havent told any of them why i keep dropping out. maybe away from the desk it'd be fine to say something.. maybe. idk i'd rather not test it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That makes sense.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: work is different tho, theres nothing to test. if my manager knew the lines were on a sticky note she'd see exactly what i already know, that i can't do the basic part. and she'd be right to stop putting me on the client stuff.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope you get a decent sleep tonight.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: doubt it lol.. already started writing next week's note. still haven't answered the saturday thing either. at work i'm the weak link and the only plan is nobody finds out. sticky note fraud.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: second client call today. same time, same sticky note.. except the client asked something that wasnt on it and i said 'let me check and get back to you' and then just sat there sweating for the rest of it. manager moved on like nothing happened. emailed the answer an hour later, nobody replied to that either. at work i can't handle one thing off-script and the note is the only thing stopping everyone from seeing it. fraud with a post-it.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sounds like a long hour.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: long hour is generous lol.. call was 30 min and i replayed the 'let me check' bit like 40 times on the bus home. its not a long-day thing tho. at work i can't think on my feet, that's just true, and if they saw how much prep goes into two lines they'd know it too.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Bus rides home after a day like that really drag.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: they do.. also skipped the board game thing saturday. sent 'sorry, next time' like an hour before. stayed in and watched a cooking show and felt kind of ok honestly? idk.. away from work it doesnt feel as much like a me problem. more like i've just been worn down for a few months and it might lift at some point. or not. hard to tell from the couch lol

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Cooking shows are a decent way to spend a Saturday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol it was a baking one, very low stakes, nobody freezing on a call. my friend sent a pic of the game after, looked fun. i almost told her why i keep bailing.. typed half of it and deleted it. maybe she'd be fine with it, idk. just didnt want to find out tonight.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That's understandable.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: work i don't even wonder about tho. if my manager knew i need a note to say 'hi, thanks for joining' she'd see the real version of me, the one who can't do the basic part of this job. and she wouldn't be wrong.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope next week's call is a quieter one.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: already writing next week's note lol, added a 'let me check' line on purpose this time.. still haven't answered her pic either. at work i'm the one who can't do it without a script and the plan is still nobody finds out. post-it fraud, week two.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: third call. note had the new 'let me check' line on it and the client didnt ask anything weird so i never even used it.. read the intro off the post-it, nodded through the rest, done in 25 min. coworker asked if i wanted to grab lunch after and i said i had to finish something, which i didnt. at work i'm someone who needs a script for 'hi' and sitting across a table from her for an hour with no note would show it. post-it fraud, week three.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Glad the call was short at least.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: short yeah.. still spent the night before rewriting the note twice and woke up at 4 running the intro in my head. the call going fine doesnt change anything tho. it went fine because the note was there. take it away and i'm the person who can't do this job, simple as that.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: 4am is a rough time to be awake.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol 4am is basically my office hours now.. on the weekend tho i slept till like 10 both days. no calls, no note, nothing to rehearse. idk, on days like that it feels less like something wrong with me and more like i've just been running on empty for months and it's catching up. maybe. or i just like sleeping in lol

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Sleeping till 10 sounds pretty nice.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it was.. finally answered my friend's game pic too. a week late, just 'looks fun!! sorry again'. she sent back a heart and asked if i'm ok and i said 'yeah just tired lately'. which is kind of true? idk. maybe she'd get the rest of it. didnt feel like testing that over text.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Nice that she checked in.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah she's like that.. work is different tho, nobody there is checking in and i'd rather keep it that way. if the lunch coworker saw me without the note she'd figure out the competent thing is fake. that's not me spiraling, it's just what would happen.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope the rest of the week's quiet.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: quiet would be good.. next call's thursday, note's already on the monitor, 'let me check' line still on it unused lol. she'll probably ask about lunch again and i'll have another fake deadline ready. at work i can't do it without the script and nobody's finding out. post-it fraud, week four incoming.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: thursday call done. client asked about the timeline so i actually had to use the 'let me check' line for the first time.. read it off the post-it word for word, voice did the wobble thing, sent the follow up email right after. lunch coworker asked again and i said i was swamped. ate a granola bar at my desk instead. at work, without the script i'm someone who can't handle a basic call and an hour across a table from her would show it. post-it fraud, week four.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: A timeline question on the spot sounds stressful.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: stressful is generous lol, i read 'let me check and get back to you' like a hostage note.. it worked because it was written down. that's the whole thing. i'm not the one who can do this part of the job, the post-it is.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Granola bar lunches are rough.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lol desk lunch champion.. saturday i went to the market tho, talked to the bread stall guy for like a minute about nothing, no script. idk. on days like that it seems more like the last few months are doing something to me than like i'm just built wrong. maybe. or bread guy is just very easy to talk to

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: That sounds like an okay Saturday.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: it was ok.. my friend sent another pic and asked if i'm still 'just tired'. said 'mostly yeah'. didnt say more. idk, she's not the type to think it's weird, maybe she'd be fine with the rest. just didnt want to find out over text.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Text is a hard place for that kind of thing.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: yeah.. work is the part i'm sure about tho. lunch coworker is nice but if she knew i rehearse 'hi' she'd stop seeing me as someone who has it together. that's not overthinking, it's just how it would go.

turns.speaker: peer
turns.text: Hope next week's a bit lighter.

turns.speaker: patient
turns.text: lighter would be nice.. next call's already on the calendar, new post-it goes up monday. she'll ask about lunch and i'll be 'swamped' again. at work i need the script and nobody's finding out. post-it fraud, week five.
